gaps.title: Default admin credentials are rejected
gaps.why: Default admin credentials give anyone full control of every staff identity.
gaps.found: The admin console accepted the default username “admin” with its default password.

breaches.title: Credential change at defined triggers
breaches.quote: require the change of authentication credentials initially, at predefined intervals and upon suspicion that the credentials were compromised

gaps.title: A recent backup snapshot exists
gaps.why: Without recent backups, ransomware or failure causes permanent data loss.
gaps.found: The newest backup was taken on 1 June 2025, 480 days ago.
gaps.should: A backup no older than 26 hours.

breaches.title: Business continuity and backup management
breaches.quote: business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management

breaches.title: Maintain backup copies of data
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall maintain backup copies of data

gaps.title: Every staff account has MFA enrolled or is forced to enrol
gaps.message: 2 account(s) without MFA: kari.admin, ola.tech; new accounts are not required to enrol OTP
gaps.action: Turn on two-factor login for every account
gaps.why: Staff accounts reach customer systems; a stolen password alone must not be enough.
gaps.found: Accounts that log in with a password alone: kari.admin and ola.tech. New accounts are not asked to set up two-factor login.
gaps.should: Every account uses two-factor login, and new accounts must set it up.

breaches.title: Multi-factor or continuous authentication
breaches.quote: the use of multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication solutions, secured voice, video and text communications and secured emergency communication systems within the entity, where appropriate.

breaches.title: Strong authentication for privileged accounts
breaches.quote: establish strong identification, authentication such as multi-factor authentication, and authorisation procedures for privileged accounts and system administration accounts;

breaches.title: Multi-factor or continuous authentication for access
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall ensure that users are authenticated by multiple authentication factors or continuous authentication mechanisms for accessing the relevant entities’ network and information systems, where appropriate, in accordance with the classification of the asset to be accessed.

gaps.title: SSH does not offer password authentication
gaps.action: Allow only key-based server logins, not passwords
gaps.why: Password logins on an admin host can be brute-forced or phished.
gaps.found: The server accepts password logins, which can be guessed or bypassed.
gaps.should: Only key-based logins (public key) are accepted.

breaches.title: HR security, access control and asset management
breaches.quote: human resources security, access control policies and asset management

breaches.title: Authentication strength matched to asset classification
breaches.quote: ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the asset to be accessed

breaches.title: Authentication strength matched to asset classification
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall ensure that the strength of authentication is appropriate for the classification of the asset to be accessed.

gaps.title: Direct root login over SSH is disabled
gaps.action: Stop direct administrator (root) logins to the server
gaps.why: Shared root logins remove individual accountability and give an attacker full control.
gaps.found: Anyone with the root password can log straight in as administrator (PermitRootLogin yes).
gaps.should: Direct root login is switched off. Administrators log in as themselves first.

breaches.title: HR security, access control and asset management
breaches.quote: human resources security, access control policies and asset management

breaches.title: Individualised and restricted administration privileges
breaches.quote: individualise and restrict system administration privileges to the highest extent possible,

gaps.title: TLS versions below the profile minimum are refused
gaps.action: Switch off outdated encryption versions on the website
gaps.why: Legacy TLS allows downgrade attacks on traffic to a public service.
gaps.found: The website still accepts TLSv1 and TLSv1.1, which are outdated and can be attacked.
gaps.should: Only TLSv1.2 or newer is accepted.

breaches.title: Cryptography and encryption
breaches.quote: policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption

gaps.title: No unaccepted, fixable vulnerability at the failing severity in running images
gaps.message: Fixable CRITICAL vulnerabilities in nginx:1.20 (17), quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3 (4), nis2lab-backup (3), grafana/loki:3.5.1 (2)
gaps.action: Update software that has known critical flaws
gaps.why: Known, fixable critical vulnerabilities are the most common way in.
gaps.found: 26 known critical flaws with an available fix, in 4 components: grafana/loki:3.5.1 (2), nginx:1.20 (17), nis2lab-backup (3) and quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3 (4). nginx:1.20 runs on an operating system that no longer gets updates.
gaps.should: No fixable critical flaws, unless a documented risk exception covers them.

breaches.title: Secure acquisition, development and maintenance; vulnerability handling
breaches.quote: security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure

breaches.title: Take measures to manage vulnerabilities
breaches.quote: take appropriate measures to manage the vulnerabilities

breaches.title: Address critical vulnerabilities without undue delay
breaches.quote: address, without undue delay, vulnerabilities identified by the relevant entities as critical to their operations

breaches.title: Apply patches within reasonable time
breaches.quote: security patches are applied within a reasonable time after they become available;

gaps.title: Every running service is in the asset inventory
gaps.message: Not in the inventory: backup, legacy-web, logs
gaps.action: Add every running service to the asset inventory
gaps.why: Unknown services go unpatched and unmonitored.
gaps.found: Running but missing from the asset inventory: backup, legacy-web and logs.
gaps.should: Every running service is listed in the asset inventory.

breaches.title: HR security, access control and asset management
breaches.quote: human resources security, access control policies and asset management

breaches.title: Maintain complete asset inventory
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall develop and maintain a complete, accurate, up-to-date and consistent inventory of their assets.

gaps.title: Incident response plan covers the NIS2 reporting stages
gaps.message: Plan does not mention: 24h early warning, 72h incident notification, one-month final report, CSIRT contact
gaps.action: Add the NIS2 reporting deadlines and the CSIRT contact to the incident plan
gaps.why: Missing a reporting deadline is itself a breach of Art. 23, separate from the incident.
gaps.found: The incident plan does not cover: 24h early warning, 72h incident notification, one-month final report and CSIRT contact.
gaps.should: The plan covers 24h early warning, 72h incident notification, one-month final report and CSIRT contact.

breaches.title: Staged reporting of significant incidents to the CSIRT
breaches.quote: without undue delay and in any event within 24 hours of becoming aware of the significant incident, an early warning

gaps.title: Brute-force protection is enabled on the staff realm
gaps.action: Turn on protection against password guessing
gaps.why: Limits online password guessing against staff accounts.
gaps.found: Nothing stops someone from guessing passwords over and over.
gaps.should: Accounts are locked for a while after repeated failed logins.

breaches.title: HR security, access control and asset management
breaches.quote: human resources security, access control policies and asset management

breaches.title: Credential reset and blocking after failed logins
breaches.quote: require the reset of authentication credentials and the blocking of users after a predefined number of unsuccessful log-in attempts

gaps.title: Password policy enforces the profile's minimum length
gaps.message: Password policy: no minimum length is set
gaps.why: Short passwords weaken the first factor even when MFA is in place.
gaps.found: No minimum password length is set.

breaches.title: HR security, access control and asset management
breaches.quote: human resources security, access control policies and asset management

breaches.title: Authentication strength matched to asset classification
breaches.quote: ensure the strength of authentication is appropriate to the classification of the asset to be accessed

breaches.title: Authentication strength matched to asset classification
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall ensure that the strength of authentication is appropriate for the classification of the asset to be accessed.

gaps.title: Central logs are kept at least as long as the profile requires
gaps.action: Keep logs for as long as the policy requires
gaps.why: Logs deleted too early make an incident impossible to investigate or report.
gaps.should: Logs are kept for at least 90 days.

breaches.title: Incident handling
breaches.quote: incident handling

breaches.title: Maintain and back up logs
breaches.quote: The relevant entities shall maintain and back up logs for a predefined period

gaps.title: Certificate is valid and not about to expire
gaps.why: An invalid certificate trains users to click through warnings, which makes interception easier.
gaps.found: The website's certificate expired on 1 January 2025.
gaps.should: A valid certificate with at least 14 days left.

breaches.title: Cryptography and encryption
breaches.quote: policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption

gaps.title: Plain HTTP redirects to HTTPS and HSTS is set
gaps.message: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS; no Strict-Transport-Security header
gaps.action: Send all website traffic over HTTPS
gaps.why: Without a redirect and HSTS, users can be kept on unencrypted HTTP.
gaps.found: Visitors who type http:// stay on the unencrypted site; browsers are not told to always use the encrypted site.
gaps.should: Visitors on http:// are sent to https://, and browsers are told to always use it.

breaches.title: Cryptography and encryption
breaches.quote: policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption

gaps.title: Incident response plan has been reviewed recently
gaps.message: Plan was last reviewed 1319 days ago
gaps.action: Review the incident response plan and record the review date
gaps.why: A stale plan lists wrong contacts and outdated systems when it is needed.
gaps.found: The incident plan was last reviewed on 14 February 2023, 1319 days ago.
gaps.should: The plan is reviewed at least every 365 days.

not_assessed.title: Annual and event-driven policy review by management
not_assessed.quote: The network and information system security policy shall be reviewed and, where appropriate, updated by management bodies at least annually and when significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks occur.

not_assessed.title: Documentation of review results
not_assessed.quote: The result of the reviews shall be documented.

not_assessed.title: Assign and revoke access rights on principles
not_assessed.quote: assign and revoke access rights based on the principles of need-to-know, least privilege and separation of duties

not_assessed.title: Modify access rights on employment change
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access rights are modified accordingly upon termination or change of employment
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Authorisation of access by relevant persons
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access to network and information systems is authorised by the relevant persons
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Control third-party access rights
not_assessed.quote: ensure that access rights appropriately address third-party access, such as visitors, suppliers and service providers, in particular by limiting access rights in scope and in duration

not_assessed.title: Maintain register of granted access rights
not_assessed.quote: maintain a register of access rights granted

not_assessed.title: Log access rights management
not_assessed.quote: apply logging to the management of access rights

not_assessed.title: Dedicated system administration accounts
not_assessed.quote: set up specific accounts to be used for system administration operations exclusively, such as installation, configuration, management or maintenance;

not_assessed.title: Administration accounts limited to administration systems
not_assessed.quote: provide that system administration accounts are only used to connect to system administration systems.

not_assessed.title: Controlled allocation of secret authentication information
not_assessed.quote: control the allocation to users and management of secret authentication information by a process that ensures the confidentiality of the information, including advising personnel on appropriate handling of authentication information
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Termination of inactive sessions
not_assessed.quote: terminate inactive sessions after a predefined period of inactivity

not_assessed.title: Separate credentials for privileged accounts
not_assessed.quote: require separate credentials to access privileged access or administrative accounts

not_assessed.title: Traceable recording of inventory changes
not_assessed.quote: They shall record changes to the entries in the inventory in a traceable manner.

not_assessed.title: Monitoring and logging procedures and tools
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall lay down procedures and use tools to monitor and log activities on their network and information systems to detect events that could be considered as incidents

not_assessed.title: Respond to detected events
not_assessed.quote: respond accordingly to mitigate the impact
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Maintain, document and review logs
not_assessed.quote: Based on the procedures referred to in point 3.2.1, the relevant entities shall maintain, document, and review logs.

not_assessed.title: List of assets subject to logging
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall establish a list of assets to be subject to logging based on the results of the risk assessment carried out pursuant to point 2.1.

not_assessed.title: Log network traffic
not_assessed.quote: relevant outbound and inbound network traffic

not_assessed.title: Log user account and permission changes
not_assessed.quote: creation, modification or deletion of users of the relevant entities’ network and information systems and extension of the permissions

not_assessed.title: Log system and application access
not_assessed.quote: access to systems and applications

not_assessed.title: Log authentication-related events
not_assessed.quote: authentication-related events

not_assessed.title: Log privileged and administrative access
not_assessed.quote: all privileged access to systems and applications, and activities performed by administrative accounts

not_assessed.title: Log critical configuration and backup file access
not_assessed.quote: access or changes to critical configuration and backup files

not_assessed.title: Log security tool events
not_assessed.quote: event logs and logs from security tools, such as antivirus, intrusion detection systems or firewalls

not_assessed.title: Log system resource use and performance
not_assessed.quote: use of system resources, as well as their performance

not_assessed.title: Log physical access to facilities
not_assessed.quote: physical access to facilities

not_assessed.title: Log network equipment and device access
not_assessed.quote: access to and use of their network equipment and devices

not_assessed.title: Log logging service state changes
not_assessed.quote: activation, stopping and pausing of the various logs

not_assessed.title: Log environmental events
not_assessed.quote: environmental events

not_assessed.title: Regular log review for unusual trends
not_assessed.quote: The logs shall be regularly reviewed for any unusual or unwanted trends.
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Alarm thresholds defined where appropriate
not_assessed.quote: Where appropriate, the relevant entities shall lay down appropriate values for alarm thresholds.

not_assessed.title: Alarm triggered on threshold exceedance
not_assessed.quote: If the laid down values for alarm threshold are exceeded, an alarm shall be triggered, where appropriate, automatically.

not_assessed.title: Timely qualified response to alarms
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall ensure that, in case of an alarm, a qualified and appropriate response is initiated in a timely manner.
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Protect logs from unauthorised access or changes
not_assessed.quote: shall protect them from unauthorised access or changes

not_assessed.title: Sufficient resources for redundancy
not_assessed.quote: provide sufficient available resources, including facilities, network and information systems and staff, to ensure an appropriate level of redundancy
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Establish backup plans
not_assessed.quote: Based on the results of the risk assessment carried out pursuant to point 2.1 and the business continuity plan, the relevant entities shall lay down backup plans which include the following:

not_assessed.title: Recovery times in backup plans
not_assessed.quote: (a) recovery times;

not_assessed.title: Completeness and accuracy of backups
not_assessed.quote: (b) assurance that backup copies are complete and accurate, including configuration data and data stored in cloud computing service environment;

not_assessed.title: Safe offsite storage of backups
not_assessed.quote: (c) storing backup copies (online or offline) in a safe location or locations, which are not in the same network as the system, and are at sufficient distance to escape any damage from a disaster at the main site;

not_assessed.title: Access controls to backup copies
not_assessed.quote: (d) appropriate physical and logical access controls to backup copies, in accordance with the asset classification level;

not_assessed.title: Restoring data from backups
not_assessed.quote: (e) restoring data from backup copies;

not_assessed.title: Backup retention periods
not_assessed.quote: (f) retention periods based on business and regulatory requirements.

not_assessed.title: Regular backup integrity checks
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall perform regular integrity checks on the backup copies.

not_assessed.title: Obtain technical vulnerability information
not_assessed.quote: obtain information about technical vulnerabilities in their network and information systems
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Evaluate exposure to vulnerabilities
not_assessed.quote: evaluate their exposure to such vulnerabilities

not_assessed.title: Monitor vulnerability information through appropriate channels
not_assessed.quote: monitor information about vulnerabilities through appropriate channels, such as announcements of CSIRTs, competent authorities or information provided by suppliers or service providers
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Vulnerability scans at planned intervals
not_assessed.quote: perform, where appropriate, vulnerability scans, and record evidence of the results of the scans, at planned intervals

not_assessed.title: Compatibility with related management procedures
not_assessed.quote: ensure that their vulnerability handling is compatible with their change management, security patch management, risk management and incident management procedures

not_assessed.title: Vulnerability disclosure procedure
not_assessed.quote: lay down a procedure for disclosing vulnerabilities in accordance with the applicable national coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy

not_assessed.title: Establish coherent security patch procedures
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall specify and apply procedures, coherent with the change management procedures referred to in point 6.4.1 as well as with vulnerability management, risk management and other relevant management procedures, for ensuring that:

not_assessed.title: Test patches before production deployment
not_assessed.quote: security patches are tested before being applied in production systems;
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Trusted sources and integrity checking
not_assessed.quote: security patches come from trusted sources and are checked for integrity;

not_assessed.title: Compensating measures when patch unavailable
not_assessed.quote: additional measures are implemented and residual risks are accepted in cases where a patch is not available or not applied pursuant to point 6.6.2.

not_assessed.title: Non-application of patches only when justified
not_assessed.quote: the relevant entities may choose not to apply security patches when the disadvantages of applying the security patches outweigh the cybersecurity benefits
not_assessed.reason: organisational requirement: needs audit, not automated checks

not_assessed.title: Document reasons for not patching
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall duly document and substantiate the reasons for any such decision.

not_assessed.title: Review policy and procedures at planned intervals
not_assessed.quote: The relevant entities shall review and, where appropriate, update the policy and procedures at planned intervals and when significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks.

not_assessed.title: Update policy and procedures where appropriate
not_assessed.quote: update the policy and procedures at planned intervals and when significant incidents or significant changes to operations or risks

not_assessed.title: Define cryptographic measures per asset classification
not_assessed.quote: in accordance with the relevant entities’ classification of assets, the type, strength and quality of the cryptographic measures required to protect the relevant entities’ assets, including data at rest and data in transit

not_assessed.title: Approve protocols, algorithms and usage practices
not_assessed.quote: based on point (a), the protocols or families of protocols to be adopted, as well as cryptographic algorithms, cipher strength, cryptographic solutions and usage practices to be approved and required for use in the relevant entities, following, where appropriate, a cryptographic agility approach

narrative.executive_summary: The scan of nordmsp-lab found 16 failing checks and no passing checks. The most severe gap: the admin console accepts the default admin/admin login (CHK-IDP-004). High-severity gaps follow: the newest backup is 480 days old (CHK-BAK-001), two staff accounts lack MFA (CHK-IDP-001), SSH offers password login and allows direct root login (CHK-SSH-001, CHK-SSH-002), outdated TLS versions are accepted (CHK-TLS-001), and running images contain fixable critical vulnerabilities (CHK-VUL-001). Medium and low gaps cover the asset inventory, incident plan content and review, login protections, log retention, and certificate and HTTPS settings (CHK-AST-001, CHK-DOC-001, CHK-IDP-002, CHK-IDP-003, CHK-LOG-001, CHK-TLS-002, CHK-TLS-003, CHK-DOC-002, CHK-SSH-003).

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require access control and that credentials are changed initially, i.e. before use. The scan logged into the admin console with the default username admin and password admin and was accepted. Default credentials are widely known, so anyone who can reach the console could take full administrative control. This requirement is not satisfied.
remediation: Change the password of the admin account on the admin console immediately so that admin/admin is rejected.
Check whether the console was accessed with these credentials and treat the account as possibly compromised.
Re-run the check to confirm the default login is no longer accepted.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require backup management and that backup copies of data are maintained. The scan found only one backup snapshot, and it is 480 days old, far beyond the maximum age the profile allows. If data were lost or corrupted today, almost everything changed since that snapshot could not be recovered, threatening business continuity.
remediation: Restore regular, automated backup runs so that a new snapshot is produced within the maximum age set in the profile.
Monitor backup jobs and alert when the newest snapshot becomes older than allowed.
Test restoring from a recent snapshot to confirm the copies are usable.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules call for multi-factor authentication, especially for privileged and administration accounts. The accounts kari.admin and ola.tech have no MFA, and new accounts are not required to enrol a one-time-password (OTP) factor. A stolen or guessed password alone would be enough to access these accounts, including what appears to be an administrator account.
remediation: Enrol MFA for kari.admin and ola.tech.
Turn on the setting that requires new users to enrol OTP (new_users_must_enrol_otp = true).
Re-run the check to confirm no account remains without MFA.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require authentication strength that matches the importance of the system. The SSH server offers password login alongside key-based login. Passwords can be guessed or reused from elsewhere, so offering them weakens remote access to the server.
remediation: Disable password authentication on the SSH server so that only publickey is offered.
Make sure keyboard-interactive and none are also not offered.
Confirm all administrators have working keys before the change.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require administration privileges to be individualised and restricted. The SSH server allows direct login as root (PermitRootLogin is 'yes'). Root is a shared, all-powerful account, so logins cannot be traced to a person and an attacker gains full control in one step.
remediation: Set PermitRootLogin to 'no' in the SSH server configuration.
Have administrators log in with personal accounts and elevate privileges only when needed.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require policies on the use of cryptography and encryption. The server still accepts TLSv1 and TLSv1.1 in addition to TLSv1.2, while the profile sets TLSv1.2 as the minimum. Accepting older versions allows connections to fall back to weaker protection of data in transit.
remediation: Configure the server to refuse TLSv1 and TLSv1.1 so that TLSv1.2 is the minimum accepted version.
Re-run the check to confirm only permitted versions are accepted.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require vulnerability handling, addressing critical vulnerabilities without undue delay and applying security patches within a reasonable time. Of 6 images scanned, 4 contain critical vulnerabilities for which a fix is available: nginx:1.20 (17), quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3 (4), nis2lab-backup (3) and grafana/loki:3.5.1 (2). No risks have been formally accepted, and nginx:1.20 runs on an operating system that is out of support. Known, fixable weaknesses are a common entry point for attackers.
remediation: Update nginx:1.20, quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.3, nis2lab-backup and grafana/loki:3.5.1 to images in which the listed CRITICAL vulnerabilities are fixed.
Replace nginx:1.20 with an image whose operating system is still supported.
Where a vulnerability cannot be fixed promptly, record a formal accepted-risk decision.
Re-scan the running images to confirm no fixable CRITICAL vulnerabilities remain.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require a complete, accurate and up-to-date asset inventory. Three running services (backup, legacy-web and logs) are not in the inventory. Services nobody has recorded tend not to be patched, monitored or owned, which leaves blind spots.
remediation: Add backup, legacy-web and logs to the asset inventory with an owner and purpose, or shut down any that are not needed.
Compare running services against the inventory regularly.

gaps.why_it_matters: NIS2 requires staged reporting of significant incidents to the CSIRT, starting with an early warning within 24 hours. The incident response plan (incident-response.md) does not mention the 24h early warning, the 72h incident notification, the one-month final report or the CSIRT contact. During an incident, staff may miss legal reporting deadlines.
remediation: Update incident-response.md to describe the 24h early warning, 72h incident notification and one-month final report.
Add the CSIRT contact details to the plan.
Brief the incident team on the updated reporting steps.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require blocking users after a predefined number of unsuccessful log-in attempts. Brute-force protection is switched off on the staff realm, so an attacker can keep guessing passwords without being blocked.
remediation: Enable brute-force protection on the staff realm (bruteForceProtected = true).
Review the failureFactor setting (currently 30) to decide how many failed attempts trigger blocking.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require authentication strength that fits the systems being accessed. No password policy is set, so there is no minimum password length, while the profile expects at least 12. Users can therefore choose very short, easily guessed passwords.
remediation: Configure a password policy with a minimum length of at least 12.
Require users with passwords that do not meet the new policy to change them.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require logs to be maintained for a predefined period to support incident handling. Central logs are deleted after 7 days, while the profile requires at least 90. Incidents are often discovered late; by then the evidence needed to investigate may already be gone.
remediation: Change the log retention period from 7 days to at least 90 days.
Make sure logs are also backed up.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require policies on the use of cryptography. The server's certificate expired on 2025-01-01. An expired certificate causes browser warnings, trains users to ignore security warnings and means visitors cannot reliably confirm they are talking to the genuine server.
remediation: Obtain and install a new, valid certificate for the server.
Set up renewal tracking or automatic renewal so the certificate is replaced well before it expires.

gaps.why_it_matters: The rules require policies on the use of encryption. Plain HTTP requests are answered directly instead of being redirected to HTTPS, and no Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header is sent. Users may use the site unencrypted, exposing data to interception.
remediation: Configure the web server to redirect all plain HTTP requests to HTTPS.
Add the Strict-Transport-Security header to HTTPS responses.

gaps.why_it_matters: Incident handling depends on a current plan. incident-response.md was last reviewed on 2023-02-14, 1319 days ago, while the profile expects a review at least every 365 days. Contacts, systems and procedures in an outdated plan may no longer be correct.
remediation: Review and update incident-response.md and record the new review date.
Schedule reviews so that the plan is never older than 365 days.

gaps.why_it_matters: Access control includes limiting login attempts. The SSH server allows 10 authentication attempts per connection, while the profile allows at most 4. More attempts per connection make guessing credentials easier.
remediation: Set MaxAuthTries to 4 or lower in the SSH server configuration.
